Design a deterministic online bin-packing heuristic. You are given the current item's size and only feasible existing bins' remaining capacities. Return one score per feasible bin; higher wins and ties choose the first bin. The evaluator opens a new bin only when no existing bin fits. Minimize the number of bins used across the search instances. You cannot see future items.

Return exactly one function: def priority(item, bins):. item is the current positive integer item size; bins is a list of feasible bin residual capacities. Return a numeric list with exactly len(bins) scores, in input order; larger scores are preferred and ties use the earliest bin. The evaluator handles feasibility and opening bins. Use only numeric local assignments, if/else, return, numeric list literals, single-generator list comprehensions over bins or numeric lists, optional comprehension filters, integer list indexing, + - * / // % **, numerical comparisons, and/or/not, and conditional expressions. Permitted calls: abs, min, max, sum, len, round, sqrt, log, exp (no keywords). No imports, attributes, strings, general loops, recursion, external state, list multiplication, generators, or other calls. Do not rebind item, bins, priority, or helper names. Use ASCII-letter-starting names of <=64 characters. All numeric intermediates must be finite with absolute value <=1e12; power requires abs(base)<=1e6 and abs(exponent)<=12; round digits are integers between -12 and 12; exp requires abs(argument)<=100. Source limit 12 KiB, AST limit 1024 nodes/depth 40, list limit 4096, evaluation limit 50000 steps. Language version: funpack-dsl-1.

Below are previously evaluated candidate functions and their search-set bin counts or mean bin count (lower is better). These are search feedback, not test-set results. Propose one useful variation.
[{"code": "def priority(item, bins):\n    return [-(r - item) / item + 0.5 * ((r - item) // item) * (len(bins) / (len(bins) + 5.0)) for r in bins]\n", "counts": [260, 264, 271, 268, 272, 289, 271, 262, 269, 271, 266, 261, 260, 255, 267, 259, 254, 262, 259, 253, 267, 263, 272, 271, 261, 265, 263, 267, 273, 263], "mean_bins": 265.26666666666665}, {"code": "def priority(item, bins):\n    return [-(r - item) - (10.0 if item / 3 < r - item <= item else 0.0) for r in bins]\n", "counts": [260, 264, 271, 268, 272, 289, 271, 262, 269, 271, 266, 260, 260, 255, 267, 259, 254, 262, 259, 253, 267, 263, 272, 271, 261, 265, 263, 267, 273, 263], "mean_bins": 265.23333333333335}]

Search memory (this run only; search-set means, lower is better): refine ratio+scaled (265.133); avoid dist+scaled (6x, 265.200); avoid scaled (5x, 265.200).

Return only the Python function in one ```python code block.

expect: response JSON object with a 'text' string: Strategy + one python block (enhanced) or one python block only (basic)
